title: Which AI investing apps are SEC-registered investment advisers?
summary: Astor, Origin, Range, Betterment and Wealthfront are offered by SEC-registered advisers. What that means, what it doesn’t, and how to check.
body_markdown:
### Is AI financial advice regulated?


Investment advice is regulated through the firm that gives it. If a registered investment adviser gives you personalized advice through an AI, that firm’s fiduciary duty and SEC rules apply. General AI tools are a different case, and OpenAI and Perplexity both say their output isn’t investment advice and shouldn’t be relied on that way.


### Does SEC registration mean the SEC approved the app?


No. Registered advisers are legally barred from implying that the SEC sponsored, recommended or approved them, and the SEC says it doesn’t endorse any firm. Registration means the firm files public disclosures, owes clients a fiduciary duty and falls under SEC oversight.


### Is ChatGPT a registered investment adviser?


No. OpenAI’s help page for Finances in ChatGPT says ChatGPT isn’t a fiduciary, registered investment adviser, broker-dealer, tax preparer or law firm, and that its responses are for informational and planning purposes. Finances also can’t make trades or move money.


### Is Robinhood Cortex investment advice?


No. Robinhood’s disclosure says Cortex Assistant isn’t an investment adviser and doesn’t provide investment advice or recommendations. It’s offered to Gold members through Robinhood Financial LLC, a broker-dealer.


### How do I look up Astor’s registration?


Search “Astor” or CRD 338424 on adviserinfo.sec.gov. The record lists the firm as Astor, also known as Gaus, Inc., registered with the SEC and based in San Francisco.
